title: Ternary Expression Parser
description:
Given a string `expression` representing arbitrarily nested ternary expressions, evaluate the expression, and return *the result of it*.

You can always assume that the given expression is valid and only contains digits, `'?'`, `':'`, `'T'`, and `'F'` where `'T'` is true and `'F'` is false. All the numbers in the expression are **one-digit** numbers (i.e., in the range `[0, 9]`).

The conditional expressions group right-to-left (as usual in most languages), and the result of the expression will always evaluate to either a digit, `'T'` or `'F'`.

examples.explanation: If true, then result is 2; otherwise result is 3.

The conditional expressions group right-to-left. Using parenthesis, it is read/evaluated as:
"(F ? 1 : (T ? 4 : 5))" --> "(F ? 1 : 4)" --> "4"
or "(F ? 1 : (T ? 4 : 5))" --> "(T ? 4 : 5)" --> "4"

The conditional expressions group right-to-left. Using parenthesis, it is read/evaluated as:
"(T ? (T ? F : 5) : 3)" --> "(T ? F : 3)" --> "F"
"(T ? (T ? F : 5) : 3)" --> "(T ? F : 5)" --> "F"

constraints: It is guaranteed that expression is a valid ternary expression and that each number is a one-digit number.
hints: Analyze the constraints and data structures appropriate for Ternary Expression Parser.
Formulate an optimal state transition or traversal invariant.
Consider corner testcases and boundary limits.
